section_summary: This section covers Japan’s fourth naval replenishment program and American assessments of what its budget might permit, while emphasizing the secrecy surrounding actual construction. Later documents report possible Italian submarine construction for Japan, Japanese oil procurement and inspection activity in North America, and uncertain observations of ships under construction at Kobe and Nagasaki.

subfiles.title: Telegram 125, section two, on Japan’s fourth naval replenishment program
subfiles.about: The embassy estimates the possible construction capacity of Japan’s fourth naval replenishment program.
subfiles.summary: A hypothetical program includes two battleships, four cruisers, two carriers, eight destroyers and submarines. Grew stresses that Japanese naval secrecy makes the estimate speculative, but naval attachés think the fourth program could support at least as much construction as the third.

subfiles.title: Confidential paraphrase of Tokyo telegram 125
subfiles.about: A paraphrase reports the fourth naval program’s budget and cautions against treating illustrative ship estimates as firm plans.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase compares allocations for warships, naval bases and air power with the third program. It repeats the attachés’ view that the new funding permits at least comparable construction despite rising costs.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs note on Tokyo despatch 3763
subfiles.about: The note summarizes the embassy’s assessment of Japan’s fourth naval replenishment program.
subfiles.summary: It highlights the program’s size, uncertain ship totals, and an attached vessel cost table.

subfiles.title: Despatch 3763 on Japan’s fourth naval replenishment program
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew compares Japan’s four naval replenishment programs and assesses the likely scale of new construction.
subfiles.summary: The despatch traces Japan’s naval programs since 1930 and links the fourth to changes in policy and circumstances after 1937. It itemizes spending on ships, bases and air power, then supplies estimated costs for several vessel types. Grew says a sample fleet of two battleships, four cruisers, two carriers, eight destroyers, eight submarines and a tender is illustrative because Japanese construction plans remain secret.

subfiles.title: More Italian armaments for Japan
subfiles.about: The consul reports negotiations for Japanese submarines at Italian yards and continuing Italian aviation support.
subfiles.summary: The report says submarine construction contracts were being drafted. It also describes aircraft exports and Italian military aviation instructors traveling to Japan.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese tanker sailing from Tuxpan
subfiles.about: The Japanese tanker Kayjo Maru is reported due to leave Tuxpan for Japan with oil.
subfiles.summary: The tanker was to sail via the Panama Canal; the report was repeated to the Navy and Coast Guard.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on Japanese Navy funding of crude oil purchase
subfiles.about: The note points to a Mexico telegram concerning an oil purchase allegedly funded by the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: It refers to 50,000 metric tons of Poza Rica crude oil and cites file 812.6363/6319.

subfiles.title: Navy Department letter on Japanese naval fuel inspectors in Los Angeles
subfiles.about: The Navy reports Japanese naval personnel assigned to inspect and supervise fuel oil purchases in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: The letter names Yatsugi, Taira and Ishimaru and says no diplomatic arrangements for an inspectorate were known to the Navy Department.

subfiles.title: Reply on the proposed Japanese naval fuel inspectorate
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Charles Edison, Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: State responds to the Navy’s report about Japanese naval inspectors stationed in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges the Navy’s letter and a Japanese Embassy note seeking tax exemptions. It says the government would not favor extending the New York naval inspector’s office to Los Angeles.

subfiles.title: Report on the launch and appearance of Zuikaku
subfiles.from: L. H. Gourley, American Consul, Kobe
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Gourley records conflicting observations about the newly launched Zuikaku at Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Observers disagree over whether the long, broad vessel is a carrier, submarine mother ship or battleship, and their size estimates vary widely. Gourley reports conflicting accounts of whether it will move to Kure or remain near Kawasaki’s Kobe facilities. He also notes a reported warship launch at Kure.

subfiles.title: Imperial Navy Adds Unit To Armada
subfiles.about: The clipping reports an Imperial Japanese Navy vessel launched on November 27.
subfiles.summary: A clipped headline and fragment report a naval launch at Kobe.

subfiles.title: Naval Construction at Nagasaki
subfiles.about: The consul assesses secret naval construction at Mitsubishi’s Nagasaki shipyards.
subfiles.summary: Two berths are screened, and three naval vessels are thought to be under construction. The consul doubts that the single large vessel is a 45,000-ton battleship, citing berth dimensions and a smaller vessel sharing the space; an aircraft carrier remains possible.
